chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Kuleyb al-Saydawi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) addressed (the people) and said in his sermon: Every intoxicant is prohibited.'

key_terms.خُطْبَتِهِ: His sermon; the address given by the Prophet
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah; referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)
key_terms.مُسْكِرٍ: Intoxicant; a substance that causes intoxication

ai.seo_question: What is the primary evidence in Shia hadith for the prohibition of all intoxicants?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the Prophet’s sermon declaring every intoxicant haram, establishing the principle of 'kathir wa qalil' (abundance and scarcity) in Shia jurisprudence. It serves as a primary textual evidence for the prohibition of any substance causing intoxication, reinforcing the Quranic concept of removing impurities. This narration is foundational for deriving the ruling on all types of intoxicants, whether consumed in small or large quantities.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Kuleyb Al Saydawi who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> addressed (the people) so he<sup>saww</sup> said in his<sup>saww</sup> sermon: ‘Every intoxicant is Prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Kulayb al-Saydawiy who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, addressed the people in which he (the Messenger of Allah) said, “Every intoxicating liquor is unlawful for consumption.’””
